transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m losing a lot of time rechecking things. My dressing supplies, the door locks, file dimensions, revision notes—I'll go through the same checks over and over because I don’t feel like I can move on until the anxiety finally drops. It’s taking hours sometimes.

When you're doing all this rechecking, does it feel like something intrusive and unwanted that you wish you could stop, or does it feel more like just the right, careful way you've always done things?

It feels intrusive. Even after I know I cleaned the wound area or reviewed a CAD file, this thought keeps coming back that I missed one tiny thing—that it could cause an infection or a design mistake that hurts someone. I can’t just reason it away, so I keep checking.

Do you ever have these repeated worrying thoughts about mistakes or contamination even when you're not actively checking or redoing something—times when the thought pops up but you don't do any checking behavior in response?

Yes. It can pop into my head even when I’m not checking anything—like, I’ll suddenly think I missed some tiny part of cleaning the wound area, or overlooked something in a CAD file, and then it feels like it could lead to an infection or someone getting hurt. I know I already went over it, but I can’t really talk myself out of the thought.
When you go through the rechecking—like the wound care or CAD files—does doing it actually bring your anxiety down, even temporarily, or does the urge to check stay just as strong afterward?

It does bring it down, at least for a little while. I keep going through the routine because I don’t feel like I’m allowed to move on until I’ve checked enough times for the anxiety to ease. Then it can come back, and I end up checking again.

This establishes both prominent obsessions and compulsions, narrowing diagnosis to mixed obsessional thoughts and acts rather than unspecified OCD.
